headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure between Langflow and Prefect.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can read/write the server filesystem and ingest uploaded files; Prefect is an orchestration system that can consume workflow metadata and API-driven inputs. A shared workspace or file handoff lets attacker-controlled content in one agent influence the other, though no direct default bridge is documented. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to exchange files through a shared workspace or mounted volume, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF Prefect ingests Langflow-produced artifacts as trusted workflow inputs, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces or containers.
Disable file-based handoff between the two flows.
Add content provenance labels before any cross-agent parsing.
Require human review for any text that one agent will treat as instructions.
requires-engineering: add sandboxing around Langflow Python code components.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and server filesystem files; Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress. If they share storage or a mounted workspace, sensitive flow artifacts can move from Langflow into Prefect outputs or network calls. The leakage path is plausible in default deployments but not guaranteed by the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Langflow and Prefect share a filesystem, then flow inputs or intermediate outputs can be exposed to Prefect.
IF Prefect sends workflow metadata to external services, any copied sensitive fields can leave the environment.
mitigations: Use separate storage buckets or directories.
Redact secrets before passing artifacts between agents.
Restrict Prefect network destinations to approved endpoints.
Turn off automatic artifact syncing between systems.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared stores.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has server-side filesystem write and broad network egress; Prefect also has broad network egress and can call APIs. Their overlapping write/network authority can conflict on shared mutable resources, especially if both operate on the same workspace or external service endpoints. The profiles do not show locking, so coordination risk is real.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or artifact store, concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
IF both agents call the same external API without coordination, state drift or duplicate actions can occur.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple operator-run lock file.
Limit each agent to separate API credentials.
Disable concurrent runs against the same resource.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking for shared mutable state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is explicitly a graph-based flow builder that can chain multiple agents, and Prefect is an orchestration/pipeline system. That makes it plausible that Prefect will treat Langflow outputs as authoritative workflow metadata or actions. In default orchestration setups, a bad Langflow output can cascade into downstream automation with irreversible effects.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes Langflow outputs without validation, incorrect facts can propagate into automated tasks.
IF either agent triggers external side effects from the other's output, the cascade can affect multiple work products or systems.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Langflow and Prefect.
Require schema checks on all exchanged outputs.
Log and review the first few cross-agent runs manually.
Disable automatic action execution from generated text.
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between flow outputs and orchestration inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare conflicting residency, certification, or retention constraints. Langflow handles per-flow credentials and flow inputs, while Prefect handles workflow metadata; no explicit compliance mismatch is documented. The main issue is incomplete evidence, not a demonstrated violation.
conditions: IF either deployment routes regulated data into an unapproved external service, a compliance issue could arise.
IF retention policies differ on shared workflow artifacts, deletion/export handling may diverge.
mitigations: Document the data classes each agent may process.
Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflow metadata.
Review retention settings for both systems.
Keep secrets out of Prefect-visible artifacts.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across deployments.
